messages.author: 78bc6c7dc041256d
messages.subject: Serial GWAS subtraction
parts:
Hello, 

I was wondering if it might be possible to perform multiple iterative subtractions. Suppose there is a GWAS summary statistic for aneurysm formation. I'd like to look for possible  "non-typical" genetic contributions to aneurysm formation after subtracting out genetic associations for "typical" risk factors for aneurysm (such as smoking, hypertension). 

Suppose my latent variables are "typical" (ie T) and "atypical" (ie AT). Then I believe my model would be:

T= ~NA*aneurysm + start(0.2)*aneurysm + start(0.2)*smoking + start(0.4)*hypertension
AT= ~NA*aneurysm + start(0.2)*aneurysm

AT~~1*AT
T~~1*T
T~~0*AT

aneurysm ~~ 0*smoking
 aneurysm~~0*aneurysm 
 smoking~~0*smoking
aneurysm~~0*hypertension
hypertension~~0*hypertension 

Per LDSC calculations, I'm planning to just run LDSC for the three traits. 

Does this sound like a reasonable approach? Do you have any advice on how I may better perform this type of analysis? 

Thank you so much for your kind help!!
Joe

messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: Serial GWAS subtraction
parts:
You'd want to do a cholesky model with 3 factors, not just two. otherwise you're controlling for a factor common to the genetic variance in the first two control variables, rather than controlling for all of the genetic variance in each control variable.

I just google imaged "cholesky model" and a 4 variable version came right up (these models are used in twin studies frequently, so examples are abundant; application within Genomic SEM is a straightforward extension).

Here it is:
https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Genetic-component-of-the-Cholesky-decomposition-model-for-oral-vocabulary-word-reading_fig1_232742608

. --

Thank you so much for your kind advice. I've been mulling over multiple references, and now have a clear understanding of your point. I've generated a model below (please refer to lavaan syntax below and schematic picture).  I believe that this model represents my goal: I'm trying to get the residual variance associated for aneurysm development (the "atypical" latent variable)  after subtracting out total variances associated with HTN or smoking. The output of the model fitting is included below.


However, I'm having difficulty with a few questions:

(2) I'm not sure why the CFI value is negative. and I'm having a tough time finding solutions online.

messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: Serial GWAS subtraction
parts:
Hi Joseph,
You will see that when you wrote your Cholesky model out you did not follow the same convention as you did in your original script in which you override the default unit loading identification (e.g. when you wrote "AT= ~NA*aneurysm + start(0.2)*aneurysm"), but you still impose a unit variance identification. Having both unit loading and unit vairance identification will overidentify your model and yield non sensible estimates for any parameters that are free. It is also likely the cause of your strange model fit (Also, your Choelsky should be fully saturated with 0 df, so you should not get model fit indices).
Try adding that NA* term to the first listed indicator of each latent variable. Then you should be set.
Cheers,
Elliot

You'd want to do a cholesky model with 3 factors, not just two. otherwise you're controlling for a factor common to the genetic variance in the first two control variables, rather than controlling for all of the genetic variance in each control variable.

I just google imaged "cholesky model" and a 4 variable version came right up (these models are used in twin studies frequently, so examples are abundant; application within Genomic SEM is a straightforward extension).
